label: Optical detector
text: Also write the UV / PDA matrix of the sample as MS:1000804 spectra (one per instant, wavelengths in nm) after the scans; off: the file is the one written without the option

label: MS-Numpress
text: Lossy MS-Numpress linear prediction of m/z and short logged float of intensities, smaller files

label: Peaks
text: file: the points the file holds (the centroids of the maker where it has them, else the profile, which the next step reduces to peaks and the run reports); profile: the profile points of the file, an error where it has none; mzlab: our own centroids, with parameters estimated on the sample and written in the mzML (MS:1000035)

label: Export inclusion list
text: Writes the m/z and RT windows of the expected products as a CSV in the columns of the inclusion list of mzFinder, sorted by RT; it adds no level and no verdict.

label: Adducts
text: Adducts of the ion table separated by commas, or a list of your own as a CSV with the header name;delta;charge;comment; one row per product and adduct; left empty it is [M-H]- for products linked in negative mode and [M+H]+ otherwise

label: RT half window
text: Each row spans the expected RT of the product plus and minus this; the start is never below 0

label: Export table as mzTab-M
text: Writes the feature table, under the view of the filter step when one is wired, as an mzTab-M 2.0 file: one small molecule and one feature per row, areas per file and per group, and an evidence for a row whose identity names a hypothesis. Every row is reliability 4 (unknown compound): the export adds no identity and raises no level.

label: Export table as CSV
text: Writes the feature table, under the view of the filter step when one is wired, as a CSV file; the column names carry the file names, so equal names give equal bytes.

label: Format
text: full: one row per feature with the summaries; full_mzmine: the same with the words of mzmine for the filled and targeted cells; quant: the areas for FBMN; csv_semicolon: the sheet of features with ;

label: Align features
text: Groups the features of all the files into rows by m/z and RT and writes the aligned table. Today one call (series::align_and_fill) does this and the filling of the gaps.

label: Family link RT
text: Family mode: largest RT distance between an ion and the root of its family in one file for the two rows to be joined

label: Family link files
text: Family mode: an ion that is mostly the base of its own family joins a family only if it follows its root in this many files

label: Coarse RT gap
text: RT gap of the coarse alignment that finds the anchors, and the widest spread of an anchor over the files: the drift between files the correction can follow

label: RT correction
text: Brings the RT of every file to a common one before the features are grouped, from anchors (peaks every file shows) found by a coarse alignment: piecewise (medians by blocks), loess (local regression), ransac (a line robust to wrong anchors); off: the RT as the files give it

label: Weak tier files
text: Features from 0.3 of the minimum height up are kept as rows only if this many files in a run show them; 0 = no weak tier

label: Detect features
text: Finds the chromatographic peaks of the MS1 scans of each file, with their quality, isotopologues and families. The parameters are common to every algorithm; each algorithm adds its own.

label: Area from
text: Xic integrates the quality trace by trapezoid on the real retention times; window sums it over the row.

label: Group representative
text: grouper only: the row of a group that is not marked as an isotopologue

label: Isotope grouping
text: averagine tests natural ratios; grouper (mzmine) groups by m/z and RT; finder (mzmine) reads each apex spectrum

label: Long trace
text: A trace longer than this is background and is not taken

label: Mass defect
text: Unit axis only: fractional part of m/z where the strong peaks pile up; measured on the file when left empty

label: Merge overlap
text: Rows within the mass tolerance are one ion when their scans overlap by this share of the shorter trace

label: RT range
text: Optional [min, max]: only rows eluting inside are kept, for every file; left empty, all rows

label: Stitch
text: Wide (default at high resolution) joins touching low pieces of neighbouring channels so a wandering ion stays one row.

label: Estimate parameters
text: Measures the noise floor, the m/z tolerance, the peak width and the dead time of each file from its own data and writes the proofs; it proposes values, the next step decides.

label: Fill gaps
text: Where a file shows no feature of a row, integrates its raw trace in the window of the row and marks the cell as filled.

label: Long trace
text: A trace longer than this is background and is not taken

label: Group ions
text: Groups the rows of a per-ion table that are one compound: same RT, heights that correlate over the files, then isotope steps and ion species that give one neutral mass. Every row stays, with a group id; the edges can go to a molecular network.

label: Apex distance
text: Largest apex distance in the shared files, as a share of the wider peak width (CAMERA perfwhm)

label: Negative ion species
text: Comma-separated species searched in negative mode, among [M-H]- [M+Cl]- [M+HCOO]- [M+CH3COO]- [M-H-H2O]- [M-2H]2- [2M-H]- [2M+HCOO]-

label: Positive ion species
text: Comma-separated species searched in positive mode, among [M+H]+ [M+Na]+ [M+NH4]+ [M+K]+ [M+H-H2O]+ [M+H-2H2O]+ [M+2H]2+ [M+H+Na]2+ [2M+H]+ [2M+Na]+ [2M+NH4]+

label: Largest charge
text: Largest charge an isotope step is read with

label: Link MS2 scans
text: Attaches to each peak the MS2 scans whose precursor lies in the peak and in the isolation window, with the purity of the precursor. Today this runs inside `features.detect` (one pass over the index), so it has no executor of its own: taking it out would change the bytes of the feature files.

label: Trigger margin
text: Seconds added on each side of the feature RT range to pair MS2 scans, 0 meaning one MS1 cycle.

label: m/z tolerance
text: Window of the peak in the MS1 scan of the precursor; at unit resolution the engine reads a negative value as Da

label: Weak purity
text: Purity below which an MS2 is weak evidence; it is not dropped

label: Import raw files
text: Recognises each vendor file set with the reader that accepts it and checks it against the limits of the platform; it changes nothing.

label: Working memory
text: Bytes of peaks held in memory while the index is built; the rest goes to a scratch file and the bytes of the index do not change

label: Correct drift
text: Brings the areas of each batch to the level of the QC files along the order of injection; refused with fewer than 5 QC files in a batch or QC files that are not at the start and the end of it. The measured areas are never overwritten.

label: Curve
text: Line or local line (LOESS) through the areas of the QC files of each batch, against the position of the injection

label: LOESS span
text: Share of the QC files of a batch in the neighbourhood of each fit; used by the local line only

label: Filter table
text: Keeps the rows that pass an ordered list of rules over the samples (campioni/2); blanks and dark files never count as samples, and a rule that cannot be evaluated is an error.

label: Keep the internal standard
text: The internal-standard row skips the blank rule, because it is spiked in the blanks too; needs the normalisation istd

label: Blank quantity
text: What is compared with the blank: area, height or normalised area; used with the sample to blank ratio only

label: Sample to blank ratio
text: The largest area of a sample is at least this many times the mean area of the blanks; needs a blank in the samples; left empty, the rule is off

label: Blank comparison
text: max_feature judges the row by its best sample; each_feature keeps it only if every sample with a peak reaches the threshold

label: Blank level
text: The blank level of a row: mean or maximum over the blank files (a blank without a peak counts as 0)

label: Subtract the blank
text: The view shows sample minus ratio times the blank level, not below 0, instead of only filtering; area or normalised area only; the ratio is at least 1 when any blank option is set

label: Duplicate m/z window
text: Of the rows within this many ppm in m/z and the duplicate RT window of each other only the one with the largest area is kept; left empty, the rule is off

label: Duplicate RT window
text: RT distance under which two rows may be duplicates; used with the duplicate m/z window only

label: Minimum files
text: Peaks found by the detection in at least this many files that are not blanks; left empty, the rule is off

label: Maximum QC CV
text: CV of the areas over the files with the role qc is at most this; a row needs a peak in at least the minimum number of them; fewer qc files than that is the error error.qc.tooFew; left empty, the rule is off

label: Minimum QC files
text: QC files with a peak that the row needs for the QC rule, and QC files that the series needs

label: Count missing QC as 0
text: The QC CV counts the QC files without a peak as 0 and the row needs no minimum of them; the series still needs the minimum number of qc files

label: Kendrick mass defect
text: KM and KMD of every ion and the series of ions that share the KMD, with their members, steps and retention trend. A series is a candidate with its evidence, never an identification.

label: Explore with PCA
text: Principal components of the samples after the blank filter, the imputation and the scaling, with the variance explained and the stability of the loadings leaving one sample out; refused under 5 samples. A view: it tests nothing.

label: Components
text: Components kept in scores and loadings

label: Scaling
text: Pareto divides by the square root of the sd; auto divides by the sd and inflates the noise with few samples

label: Plausibility of the values
text: Seven checks of the numbers the table shows: finite values, m/z and RT inside a real run, no negative area or height, a width and an apex for every detected peak, rows with no peak in any file and the ppm error of the identity columns. Numbers only: a flagged row is a value to look at, never a verdict.

label: Alignment tolerance
text: 0.1 Da or more is unit resolution and the ppm error is not read; without a value the recipe stored in the table decides

label: Largest ppm error
text: A row whose m/z is further than this from its neutral mass plus adduct is flagged; read only in a high-resolution table

label: Compare conditions
text: Welch's t on log2(area + pseudocount) for each comparison of the design and a one-way ANOVA over all the conditions, with Benjamini-Hochberg q-values and log2FC; refused with a reason and no number when a condition has fewer than 3 files. The p-values stay in this output: no view shows them.

label: Pseudocount
text: Added to every area before the logarithm and in the log2FC; without a value it is 3 x the median of the positive areas of the blanks, else of the reference, else the floor

label: Aquatic hazard
text: One acute and one chronic aquatic hazard category per chemical identity, from versioned snapshots read from the campaign folder with their hash, no network. A hazard class is a property of a structure, not a risk: no concentration, no PNEC. A Level 3 identity carries the caveat of its candidate structure.

label: Identification level
text: Gives each feature the level its evidence reaches (1, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b, 4, 5; 0 = detected, not annotated), with the basis and the reasons. Level 1 only with a standards file of yours; suspect fragments of screen.suspects give 3a. Level 2b is never given by the program: the chemist decides it. A CANOPUS class gives no level: it is a separate annotation.

label: Class probability
text: A CANOPUS class is shown, as an annotation of its own that gives no level, at or above this probability

label: COSMIC confidence
text: Confidence of the Level 3 gate; 0.64 is the threshold of the COSMIC paper, roughly an FDR of 10 %, a practical guide and no guarantee

label: Conflicting libraries
text: best_match: the libraries are one library; level3: sources naming different structures give Level 3

label: Conflict margin
text: The best match keeps Level 2a only if its cosine exceeds the best match of a different structure by this much

label: Standard MS2 score
text: Level 1: the MS2 score (entropy similarity, or cosine for a cosine hit) of the hit on the standard

label: Regulatory lists
text: Compares the identities with the regulatory package by InChIKey: the same full key is a match, the same first block a flagged match, a name or a formula never. A list entry says what a compound is on a list, nothing about this sample; no network.

label: Mass window
text: Entries of the lists outside this range of monoisotopic mass are left out; absent: all the entries

label: Formula from MS1
text: Candidate molecular formulas of each feature from the exact mass and, when the isotope finder finds a pattern, from the isotope pattern. The list is ordered by score and by a confidence that is a share of the list, never an identification: the chosen formula is the chemist's.

label: Elements
text: Ranges as C:0-50,H:0-100. Absent: C:0-50,H:0-100,N:0-8,O:0-15,P:0-2,S:0-3 plus the heavy elements the finder sees in the spectrum; the text given is searched as written

label: Charge
text: Absent: the isotope finder decides, and 1 when it finds no pattern; above 1 the formulas are those of the ion itself

label: Formula from MS2
text: Assigns to each cleaned peak the closest sub-formula of the ion of the candidate formula and gives the neutral losses. A sub-formula supports the FORMULA, never the structure: isomers share it.

label: Sub-formula limit
text: Above this many sub-formulas the table is not built and the candidate explains no fragment; memory grows with the limit

label: Precursor tolerance
text: Precursor against the ion of the formula, the adduct with the smallest error of the polarity

label: Retention time plausibility
text: Compares the retention time of a candidate with what the campaign's own confident identifications predict. A warning aid that ranks or doubts a candidate: it never applies a level and does not tell isomers apart.

label: Order
text: residual: within each query the candidates with the smallest |residual| first; a candidate without a prediction last

label: Parent RT
text: With a parent: the direction of the RT change (rt_dir) and whether it agrees with delta_logp (rt_dir_agrees)

label: Find suspects
text: Searches the aligned feature table in the suspect lists you give by neutral mass for each adduct. Listed structures with the same formula are one isomer group, never one name. A regulatory package adds the lists naming each candidate. Candidates with their evidence, Level 5 (mass and formula) or 4 (also a candidate formula); no verdict.

label: Regulatory lists
text: Ids of the lists of a regulatory package to screen, comma-separated; empty: every list in force

label: Handle chimeric MS2 spectra
text: Finds the other ions co-isolated in the precursor window of each MS2 spectrum, writes the purity of the precursor and the intruders, and leaves the spectrum as it is: the scores that read it discount the peaks an intruder can explain. Nothing is removed from the spectrum.

label: In silico fragmentation
text: Breaks each candidate structure of a local list bond by bond and ranks it by the weight of the peaks its fragments explain. The candidates are a CSV list with PubChemLite columns, the structures of a screen.suspects result, or the in-silico package (PubChemLite, CC BY 4.0) downloaded once on a click and read by mass window. The result is a hypothesis with its proofs (peaks explained, mass error), never an identity. No network at analysis time.

label: Score terms
text: On: every candidate also carries score_terms, its score as the share of each explained peak and the key of its formula in the Theory; the scores themselves do not change

label: Compare MS2 spectra
text: Scores each query MS2 spectrum against a spectral library inside the precursor window and keeps the best candidates per feature. A candidate is a hit with its scores and shared peaks, never an identity: the level is decided by annot.level.

label: Library adduct contains
text: Only library entries whose adduct (for example [M+H]+) contains this text (any case) are candidates; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Library collision energy contains
text: Only library entries whose collision energy text contains this text (any case) are candidates, for example 30 or HCD; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Decoys
text: spectrum: a decoy spectrum (random fragments, same intensities) is searched beside every library entry and each best hit carries decoy_q, the q-value of the batch; it is a lower bound of the true error rate (isomers and analogues are not random errors). Works with the entropy, cosine and modified cosine scores (not tree; the q-value counts the candidates inside the precursor window; an .mzlib is read back to spectra and rebuilt with the decoys); none leaves the hits as they are

label: Library instrument contains
text: Only library entries whose instrument or instrument type contains this text (any case) are candidates, for example Orbitrap or QTOF; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Matched peaks
text: On: every candidate also lists matched_peaks, the pairs of peaks behind its score (m/z and relative intensity of the query and of the library spectrum, and whether the precursor shift was needed), so the match can be checked peak by peak; the scores do not change. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Library name contains
text: Only library entries whose name contains this text (any case) are candidates; empty keeps all. The spectra still decide the score

label: Precursor window (low resolution)
text: Precursor window in Da for unit-resolution data; 0 keeps the ppm window, or 0.7 Da for a unit-resolution file.

label: RT tolerance
text: Above 0, a library entry whose retention time differs from the RT of the query spectrum by more than this is not a candidate; entries or queries without a retention time are kept. The candidate carries rt_delta_min (query minus library) when both are known; 0 switches the filter off. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Score terms
text: On: every candidate also carries score_terms, its score as a weighted sum of named terms (the contribution of each matched pair, the rest in one term) and the key of its formula in the Theory; the scores themselves do not change

label: Fragment tolerance (ppm)
text: Above 0 it replaces tol_da: a peak pairs within this many ppm of its own m/z (high-resolution spectra); the analogue search uses it too

label: Transition table
text: Matches each row of a table of SIM ions or SRM transitions to the chromatograms of each file at unit resolution and integrates the peak inside its RT window: area, height, apex RT, S/N and a flag when there is no peak. For rows without an RT it lists candidate peaks sorted by area; it never says which isomer a peak is.

label: Peaks of the UV trace
text: Integrates the peaks of the UV/PDA trace of each file at one wavelength: apex, edges, width, height and area. With broad bands on it also finds the bands that the narrow peak finder loses. It lists peaks; it does not identify.

label: Wavelength
text: The trace is the matrix at this wavelength; the nearest column when none is inside the band

label: Export annotations
text: Writes one CSV with, for every feature, the candidates of every identification method of the plan side by side (standard, library, in silico, suspect, formula), each with its own score and name, and the level and reason annot.level gave. It adds no identity and raises no level.

label: Feature table
text: Indexes the files, detects the features of each, aligns them and writes the table as CSV: the chain of `mzlab-cli features` as one step.

label: Compare algorithms
text: Runs the wrapped step once per variant on the same inputs and measures how the outputs differ; it does not say which variant is right.

label: MSn graph as a figure
text: Draws the fragmentation graph as an SVG, a stand-alone HTML or a PNG: ions with m/z, relative intensity, MS levels and the proposed formulas, arrows for the neutral losses. The formulas are candidates of the graph, not identifications.

label: Format
text: svg: the static figure, colours written in the file; html: one file with no external resource, two views, data table and downloads; png: the SVG rasterised (only in a build with the cargo feature `png`)

label: View
text: tree: columns by MS level; radial: the precursor in the centre, one ring per step of the best path (the HTML has both and opens on this one)

label: MSn tree as a library
text: Writes the spectra of the fragmentation graph as an MSP or MassBank library, one record per spectrum of the tree, with the proposed formula and the neutral loss of each explained peak. The formulas are candidates of the graph, not identifications.

label: Annotate peaks
text: Write the sub-formula of each explained peak and the neutral loss from its precursor (MSP: quoted note; MassBank: PK$ANNOTATION and a COMMENT)

label: MS levels
text: all: one record per spectrum of the tree, MS2 and deeper; ms2: only the spectra of the first fragmentation

label: MSn graph as a table
text: Writes the fragmentation graph as CSV: its ions with the proposed sub-formulas, its modifications (neutral losses between ions) or its peaks. The formulas are candidates of the graph, not identifications.

label: Table
text: modifications: one row per neutral loss between two ions of the tree (mass, formula, ppm, measures); nodes: one row per ion with its proposed sub-formula; peaks: one row per peak of every spectrum with its node

label: Mass accuracy
text: Measures the mass error of each file on ions that are known to be there (the lab background list, internal standards and standards of the user) and reports offset, spread, standards and warnings; with a model it also writes a copy of the feature table with its m/z corrected. Numbers only, no verdict.

label: Check run order
text: Reads the sample table and reports, for each batch, the number of files of each role, the largest gap between two QC injections, the blanks and the distinct standard levels, with a warning for a gap above the limit, a batch without QC or blank, too few standard levels, and a missing or repeated injection order. It reports facts, never a verdict.

label: Calibrate
text: Applies imported calibration curves (signal = slope x concentration + intercept) to the signal of the matched rows of the table; concentrations outside the linear range or below zero are flagged. The line is not fitted here.

label: Calibration curve
text: Fits weighted calibration lines to the standards, back-calculates every standard and unknown, gives LOD and LOQ.

label: Points left out of the fit
text: analyte|sample|reason separated by semicolons; * as analyte = every analyte; each one is logged.

label: Methods text
text: Writes the methods of a run in English from its run record: every step with its version, algorithm and parameters, and the version of mzLab. It states what was set, never a result.

label: Centroid the spectra
text: Reduces every profile scan of an mzML to one point per peak with the centroider of the archive; centroid scans, chromatograms and a file with no profile scan are left as they are.

label: Threshold
text: A peak is kept when it stands this many sigma over the background (Poisson Z for counts); left out, the value of the mode of the file

label: Find spectra in a library
text: Writes the entries of the library you declare that have a given name, formula, InChIKey, accession or precursor m/z, with their peaks untouched, so that the next steps can use them as queries. The library is always the one you supply: nothing is built in and nothing is searched online.

label: Look up by
text: The field of the library entries that value is compared with; precursor_mz takes a number and the window ppm

label: Whole name
text: By name: the name must be the whole value, not only contain it (any case); the other fields are always compared whole

label: Entries kept
text: The first entries in the order of the library; the rest are not written

label: MS2 spectra from mzML
text: Reads the MS2 scans of data-dependent runs and writes them as spectra with precursor m/z and intensity, charge, RT and scan number; given a feature table it keeps the scans of its features and names each spectrum with the feature id.

label: Fragment correlation
text: With `dia_pseudo`: least Pearson correlation between the trace of a fragment and that of the precursor

label: Cycles per peak
text: With `dia_pseudo`: fewest cycles of the RT range of a feature; a feature with fewer has no spectrum

label: DIA pseudo spectra
text: For data-independent runs (SWATH, MSE): one pseudo MS2 spectrum per feature of the table, made of the fragments whose trace follows that of the precursor; needs the feature table, and the DDA scans are not written

label: Largest isolation window
text: Scans whose isolation window is wider are dropped; off when absent, and a scan that does not say its window is kept

label: MSn fragmentation graph
text: Merges the MSn spectra of an infusion into one graph of ions and neutral losses, with the sub-formulas of the fragments when the ion of the root is given. It proposes candidates; it does not identify.

label: Trap cut-off q
text: Fragments below q/0.908 of the precursor m/z are treated as not observable.

label: Node to cleave
text: Node (nK) whose m/z is explained by structure cleavages; all for all nodes of level 2 or more.

label: Contains moiety
text: Keeps the rows of a candidate table whose structure contains a moiety (or the ones that lack it) and writes the number of its matches in a last column. A row kept is a candidate that holds the group, never an identification.

label: Compare the MS2 of the table rows
text: Takes the MS2 spectrum of every row of the aligned table, as the MGF export does, and scores it against a spectral library like spectra.match: the candidates of each row carry the score, the shared peaks, the decoy q-value and the name. A candidate is never an identity: the level is decided by annot.level.

label: Library adduct contains
text: Only library entries whose adduct (for example [M+H]+) contains this text (any case) are candidates; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Library collision energy contains
text: Only library entries whose collision energy text contains this text (any case) are candidates, for example 30 or HCD; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Decoys
text: spectrum: a decoy spectrum (random fragments, same intensities) is searched beside every library entry and each best hit carries decoy_q, the q-value of the batch; it is a lower bound of the true error rate (isomers and analogues are not random errors). Works with the entropy, cosine and modified cosine scores (not tree; the q-value counts the candidates inside the precursor window; an .mzlib is read back to spectra and rebuilt with the decoys); none leaves the hits as they are

label: Library instrument contains
text: Only library entries whose instrument or instrument type contains this text (any case) are candidates, for example Orbitrap or QTOF; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Matched peaks
text: On: every candidate also lists matched_peaks, the pairs of peaks behind its score (m/z and relative intensity of the query and of the library spectrum, and whether the precursor shift was needed), so the match can be checked peak by peak; the scores do not change. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Take out the blank background
text: On: the MS2 peaks that recur in the blank files are taken out of every row, never the precursor; without a blank file nothing is taken out

label: Spectrum of a row
text: best: the scan with the highest TIC of the file that has the best MS2 of the row; consensus: all the fitting scans of the row, merged across the files where it has a peak

label: Library name contains
text: Only library entries whose name contains this text (any case) are candidates; empty keeps all. The spectra still decide the score

label: Precursor window (low resolution)
text: Precursor window in Da for unit-resolution data; 0 keeps the ppm window, or 0.7 Da for a unit-resolution file.

label: RT tolerance
text: Above 0, a library entry whose retention time differs from the RT of the query spectrum by more than this is not a candidate; entries or queries without a retention time are kept. The candidate carries rt_delta_min (query minus library) when both are known; 0 switches the filter off. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Score terms
text: On: every candidate also carries score_terms, its score as a weighted sum of named terms (the contribution of each matched pair, the rest in one term) and the key of its formula in the Theory; the scores themselves do not change

label: Fragment tolerance (ppm)
text: Above 0 it replaces tol_da: a peak pairs within this many ppm of its own m/z (high-resolution spectra); the analogue search uses it too

label: Dig the unit-resolution series
text: Scores the products a parent can form in a series at unit resolution: peaks checked on their XIC, persistence, growth, blanks, chance. It proposes candidates; it does not identify.

label: Draw a structure
text: Opens the structure editor (Ketcher, in a sandboxed frame inside the page) so the student draws the parent or a product. A partial structure carries a Δ in a bracket or an attachment on any atom of a ring, which makes it a level 3 candidate and never an identification.

label: Reactivity of the parent
text: Computes where the parent is most reactive toward an electrophilic radical (condensed Fukui function f(-) per atom and per class of C-H sites). The result is a prior shown beside the sites of tp.position and never decides one: the experiment does.

label: Conformers
text: ETKDG conformers of the parent, lowest energy first; f(-) is also computed on the lowest ones to give its spread

label: Form of the parent
text: none: the SMILES as written; ph7: the most probable charge form at pH 7 from a table of typical pKa

label: Draw the modification
text: Chooses the simplest form that tells the truth about a product: the structure itself only when the position is a site, a multicenter bond when every candidate lies in one aromatic ring, otherwise a bracket around a zone or the whole parent. Never one structure per site. The page draws it over the coordinates of the parent that Ketcher gives; without them the structure becomes a bracket.

label: Filters of the products
text: Hides a row for the first filter it fails: F1 peak quality, F2 isotopologue of another row, F3 as strong in the controls as in the treated samples, F4 constant ratio to the parent (in-source fragment or adduct), F5 formula error beyond the tolerance of the file. Rows are marked, not deleted. The decoys (rule deltas shifted by a mass defect) say how many matches are by chance.

label: Lowest formula tolerance
text: Floor of the tolerance of a formula; the tolerance of a file is its measured error, kept between the two

label: Hypotheses of the products
text: Lists the ions that the chemistry says could be there, each with the source that proposed it: the parent times the photocatalytic rules (one or two steps), the offline suspect index, the expected members of the families already found, and lists the user typed or imported. One pass, fixed order, byte-identical on every run. A hypothesis is a place to look and what the search finds is graded afterwards.

label: Chained reactions
text: Most reactions chained from the parent; one hypothesis per net change of formula, the fewest steps first

label: Most suspects
text: Hypotheses taken from the suspect index, the best supported first; the number left out is written in the registry

label: Unit resolution
text: Two formulas of the same nominal m/z and adduct are one hypothesis, the others its alternatives

label: Other polarity too
text: Expected members of a family in the other polarity too ([M-H]- of a positive base and the reverse)

label: Link the MS2 of the products
text: Gives each row that passes the filters the modification it carries (formula change from the parent and isotope check of the MS1 at the apex), every DDA MS2 of its series with the purity of the isolation, and the comparison of the fragments with the MS2 and the MSn tree of the parent. Evidence for the chemist: it never names the product.

label: Formula tolerance
text: Tolerance of the modification (neutral formula change) and of the comparison of the fragments with the parent

label: Polarity
text: Polarity of the series: the adduct of the parent and the MS1 scans read for the purity

label: Lowest purity
text: A scan below this purity is chimeric and does not vote

label: Isolation centre
text: An MS2 scan belongs to a row when its isolation centre is within this many ppm of the m/z of the row

label: Network of the products
text: Draws the parent and the accepted products in columns by the number of steps from the parent, with an arc wherever a rule of the transformation table takes the ion formula of one to that of another. The source of an arc is the product that peaks first; an arc from the parent carries the fragments of the MS2 that are equal or shifted by the change. A network is evidence of kinship and never an identification: it raises no level.

label: Fewest shared fragments
text: An arc from the parent whose MS2 was compared is kept with at least this many fragments in common, equal or shifted; 0 keeps every arc

label: Position of the modification
text: Says which classes of sites of the parent the MS2 of a product is compatible with, never which site it is: classes are excluded, supported or undistinguished, the sublevel is 3a only when at least one class is excluded and at most three remain, and the rest is 3b. The reactivity of the parent is shown beside as a prior and does not decide.

label: Margin of the lead
text: Log-likelihood units a class must lead the second by to be called alone: two fragments' worth of evidence

label: Decide the levels
text: Keeps what the chemist decides for each row: a level, a note of up to 200 characters, or not a TP. The programme proposes and shows the evidence; a decision is allowed by the rules of the levels (2b only on a row proposed at 2a, 3a, 3b or 4; 1 only with a standard marked) and a refused one is listed with its reason and not counted. It decides nothing by itself.

label: Convert to mzML
text: Writes the spectra of each sample as mzML; the version of this step names the writer.

label: Compression level
text: zlib level of the binary arrays, 0 (none) to 9 (smallest)

label: Family row span
text: Family mode: largest RT span of the groups joined in one row

label: Rows
text: One row per family of ions (isotopologues, adducts, in-source fragments) or one per ion

label: m/z tolerance
text: At unit resolution the engine reads a negative value as Da

label: RT gap
text: Largest gap of RT between neighbouring features of one row

label: RANSAC distance
text: Largest distance of an anchor from the line to agree with it (ransac)

label: RANSAC seed
text: Seed of the random samples of the line (ransac); the same seed gives the same correction

label: LOESS span
text: Fraction of the anchors each local fit takes (loess)

label: Split gap
text: A row with two features of one file (close isomers) is cut at the RT gaps above this

label: m/z tolerance (Da)
text: Unit axis only; left empty, the recipe of the file (measured window or 0.35 Da)

label: Finder absolute tolerance
text: finder only: absolute lower bound of the m/z tolerance

label: Heavy elements from the spectrum
text: finder only: Cl, Br, S and Si seen in the spectrum widen the expected pattern

label: Finder elements
text: finder only: comma-separated elements whose isotopes are looked for

label: Finder largest charge
text: finder only: the charges tried, from 1 up to this

label: Finder m/z tolerance
text: finder only: m/z tolerance in the spectrum, the larger of this and the absolute one

label: Require a 13C peak
text: finder only: a charge counts only with a 13C peak

label: Noise floor
text: Points below are ignored; left empty, it is estimated from the intensity histogram

label: Isotope absolute tolerance
text: grouper only: absolute lower bound of the m/z tolerance

label: Isotope largest charge
text: grouper only: the charges tried, from 1 up to this

label: Only heavier isotopes
text: grouper only: look only above the start row

label: Isotope m/z tolerance
text: grouper only: m/z tolerance of an isotope step, the larger of this and the absolute one

label: Isotope RT tolerance
text: grouper only: largest RT distance of an isotopologue to the start row

label: Maximum gap
text: Scans a trace may miss between two of its points; 0 = consecutive scans

label: Minimum S/N
text: A feature whose apex is below this many times the noise of its flanks is dropped; 0 = off

label: Minimum width
text: Drops features narrower than this share of the typical peak width of the file; 0 = off

label: Polarity
text: 1 positive, -1 negative, 0 all MS1 scans

label: Polarity
text: 1 positive, -1 negative, 0 all MS1 scans

label: Maximum gap
text: Scans a trace may miss between two of its points; 0 = consecutive scans

label: m/z tolerance
text: At unit resolution the engine reads a negative value as Da

label: RT tolerance
text: Half width added to the window of RT

label: m/z tolerance (Da)
text: Unit axis only; left empty, the recipe of the file (measured window or 0.35 Da)

label: Height correlation
text: Smallest Pearson correlation of the heights of two rows over the files (CAMERA cor_eic_th)

label: Files for the correlation
text: The heights are compared only when both rows are measured in at least this many files

label: Smallest m/z tolerance
text: Floor of the m/z tolerance at low mass

label: Polarity
text: Which list of ion species is searched; auto = the polarity of the files of the table

label: RT tolerance
text: Largest distance between the RT of two rows of one compound

label: Default isolation half window
text: Used when the index records no isolation window; the peak is then marked as estimated

label: m/z tolerance (Da)
text: Unit axis only; left empty, the recipe of the file (measured window or 0.35 Da)

label: Build scan index
text: Reads the scans of each sample once and writes the .mzidx the later steps read in slices.

label: Blank cells
text: Which blank cells set the blank level: only the detected ones, or the gap-filled ones too.

label: Blank matching
text: Compare each sample only with the blanks of its batch or matrix; others use all blanks.

label: Duplicate m/z window (Da)
text: Of rows this many Da apart in m/z and close in RT, only the strongest is kept.

label: Internal standard row
text: Id of the row of the internal standard; used with the normalisation istd

label: Internal standard m/z
text: m/z of the internal standard; with its RT, the nearest row is the standard.

label: Internal standard RT
text: RT of the internal standard; used with its m/z

label: Minimum area
text: The largest area over the files is at least this; left empty, the rule is off

label: Minimum height
text: The largest height over the files is at least this; left empty, the rule is off

label: Minimum replicate fraction
text: Kept if some replicate group has the row detected in at least this fraction of its files.

label: Normalisation
text: Scale each file by its total area, its median area or the area of the internal standard.

label: Require MS2
text: An MS2 is linked to the peak; left empty, the rule is off

label: Minimum members
text: Distinct nominal Kendrick masses a series needs

label: KMD window
text: Width of the KMD window of a series

label: Repeating unit
text: Unit of the Kendrick mass

label: Blank factor
text: A feature must exceed the blank level times this factor; skipped when no file is a blank

label: Files above the blank
text: Sample files that must exceed the blank threshold

label: Minimum area
text: Smallest maximum area of a feature, and the area that counts as present

label: Minimum samples present
text: Samples in which a feature must be present

label: Blank level
text: Level of the blank files: the maximum or the mean of their areas

label: Transform
text: log2 of the areas after the imputation, or the areas as they are

label: Highest m/z
text: A row above it is flagged

label: Lowest m/z
text: A row below it is flagged: no LC-MS run reads there

label: Longest run
text: A row with an RT outside 0 and this value is flagged: check the unit of the times

label: Widest peak
text: A detected peak wider than this, or with no width or apex, is flagged

label: Pseudocount floor
text: Smallest estimated pseudocount, and the one used when no file gives a noise level

label: Putative library entries
text: Library entries named Spectral Match to ... (propagated annotations) are taken to Level 3

label: RT group
text: Features of one identity farther apart in RT (consecutive) are different peaks

label: Shared fragments
text: Shared fragment ions of a library match, every library (SIRIUS, GNPS2, mzMine)

label: Library cosine
text: Cosine of a library match, every spectral-library source

label: Standard mass tolerance
text: Level 1: the precursor of the hit on the standard

label: Standard RT window
text: Level 1: the feature RT is within this of the RT of the standard you gave

label: Suspect fragments
text: Level 3a: at least this many fragments listed for a suspect are found in the feature MS2

label: Also compare
text: Statuses added to the lists in force: proposal, draft, reference; empty: none

label: Regulatory lists
text: Ids of the lists to compare, comma-separated; empty: every list in force

label: Highest charge tried
text: Charges the isotope finder looks at

label: Require 13C peak
text: The isotope finder accepts a pattern only with the 13C peak

label: Fragment tolerance
text: Fragment against a sub-formula of the ion (the MS2 tolerance of SIRIUS)

label: Drop outside the window
text: On: the candidates whose RT falls outside the window are removed (logp_window only)

label: Parent structure
text: SMILES of the parent compound: each candidate then gets delta_logp (Crippen) against it

label: logP margin
text: A change of logP within this margin gives no direction

label: RT margin
text: A change of RT within this margin gives no direction

label: Adducts
text: Comma-separated; the ones of the polarity of the table are searched

label: Also screen
text: Statuses added to the lists in force: proposal, draft, reference; empty: none

label: Formulas per feature
text: Most formula groups kept per feature, the closest in mass first

label: Fragments needed
text: Keeps a candidate only if this many of its listed fragments are in the MS2; off when empty

label: MS2 RT tolerance
text: Without feature ids in the spectra: largest RT distance between a scan and the feature

label: RT window
text: Drops a candidate whose listed RT is farther than this from the feature; off when empty

label: Mass tolerance
text: Candidates within this of the neutral mass of the precursor

label: Bonds broken
text: A candidate is broken bond by bond up to this many bonds

label: Precursor tolerance
text: Library precursor against the precursor of the feature

label: Fragment tolerance
text: Fragment window in Da; 0 follows the query: 0.02 Da, or 0.5 Da for a unit-resolution file.

label: Baseline
text: Down to zero, or the line between the edges.

label: RT gap of a group
text: Candidate apexes of different files closer than this are one candidate (candidates output)

label: Candidates per trace
text: Most candidate peaks taken from the trace of each file (candidates output)

label: Min. points per peak
text: A peak with fewer points above 5 % of its height is reported as no_peak

label: m/z tolerance
text: A chromatogram belongs to a row when its Q1 (and Q3) are within this of the row's

label: Output
text: Long list, one row per transition, or candidate peaks.

label: RT half window
text: The peak is searched in RT plus and minus this when the row writes no window

label: Smoothing
text: 1 = none, 3 = 1-2-1, 5 = 1-4-6-4-1 before the apex and the edges are found

label: S/N noise
text: Read the noise on the raw trace, or on the smoothed one.

label: Min. S/N
text: A peak under this signal-to-noise is reported as no_peak

label: Transition table
text: One row per SIM ion or SRM transition; leave RT empty to look for candidates.

label: Bandwidth
text: The columns within half of this around the wavelength are averaged

label: Broad bands
text: Also look for bands too wide for the narrow peak finder

label: Widest band
text: Largest full width at half maximum of a band

label: Narrowest band
text: Smallest full width at half maximum of a band

label: Min. S/N of a band
text: Smallest height of a band over its bridge, in noise units

label: Lowest level
text: Write only features at this level or better; empty = all.

label: Separator
text: comma: the usual CSV; semicolon: for spreadsheets with a decimal comma

label: Candidates per method
text: Candidates kept per feature and method.

label: Explained peaks only
text: Keep only the peaks a node of the graph explains

label: Format
text: MSP, or MassBank records (MS_TYPE MS2, MS3, ... and the path of precursors in the comment)

label: Record name
text: Name of the records; empty = the formula of the ion of the root, or MSN

label: Explained peaks only
text: peaks table only: keep the peaks a node of the graph explains

label: Blank in every batch
text: Report a batch with no blank.

label: Largest gap between QC injections
text: Report two QC files that are further apart than this.

label: Standard levels per batch
text: Report a batch with fewer distinct standard concentrations.

label: Internal standard
text: One name for every analyte, or analyte|IS pairs separated by semicolons; empty = none.

label: Calibration model
text: quadratic: the ICH LOD/LOQ (3.3σ/b, 10σ/b) use b, the slope at zero concentration.

label: Weighting of the standards
text: 1/x and 1/x2 leave out a standard at zero concentration; the log says so.

label: Force the line through zero
text: true or false; any other value fails the step.

label: Layout
text: paragraph: one English paragraph per step; list: one bullet per step with every parameter

label: Peak width
text: FWHM of a peak; left out, it is measured on the isolated peaks of the file

label: Precursor window
text: By precursor_mz: the entries whose precursor is this close to the value

label: Value
text: The text to find (for precursor_mz, the m/z); required

label: Fragment tolerance
text: With `dia_pseudo`: window around an m/z to follow its trace

label: Peak threshold
text: Peaks below this intensity are dropped; a scan left with no peak is dropped

label: RT tolerance
text: With a feature table: largest distance between the scan and the RT of the feature

label: Precursor tolerance
text: With a feature table: largest distance between the precursor and the m/z of the feature

label: Activation
text: Keep only spectra of this activation (cid, hcd, ...); empty keeps all.

label: Adduct
text: Adduct of the root ion, e.g. [M+H]+ or [M-H]-.

label: Break the bonds
text: Add the atom sets of the structure, with bonds cut, that give the m/z of each node.

label: Root ion
text: Formula of the root ion, e.g. C13H24N4O3S+H; leave empty for masses only.

label: Hydrogens moved
text: Maximum number of hydrogens moved beyond the plain cleavage.

label: Interpret losses
text: Add to each arc the neutral loss, its mass error and the activations that saw it.

label: Keep M+1 peaks
text: Turn the M+1 peaks of fragments into nodes linked to their monoisotopic peak.

label: Loss window
text: Maximum distance in ppm, relative to the precursor m/z, for matching a loss by mass.

label: Rule tolerance
text: Maximum distance in mDa between a loss and the mass of a rule.

label: Low m/z limit
text: Below this m/z the wider low-mass window may apply.

label: Bonds cut
text: Maximum number of bonds cut for one piece, 1 or 2.

label: Evidences for the wider window
text: Number of evidences a candidate needs to use the wider window.

label: Molecule
text: Name, synonym, id or formula to look up in the molecules list.

label: Structure (molfile)
text: 2D structure as a molfile, stored in the graph for the drawings.

label: Chosen formulas
text: Pairs MZ=ION separated by commas, fixing the formula of the node at that m/z.

label: Sub-formula window
text: Maximum distance in ppm between a fragment m/z and a candidate sub-formula.

label: Apply fragmentation rules
text: Add the rule that explains each loss, the even-electron check and the trap cut-off.

label: Structure (SMILES)
text: SMILES of the molecule, stored in the graph for the drawings.

label: Cleavage window
text: Maximum distance in ppm between a cleaved piece and the m/z of the node.

label: Low-mass window
text: Wider ppm window used below the low m/z limit when enough evidences support the candidate.

label: SMILES column
text: Header of the column with the SMILES of each row, compared without case

label: Rows kept
text: Keep the rows with the moiety, or the rows without it.

label: Moiety
text: The substructure every row kept must contain.

label: Match stereo
text: The stereo of the moiety must match too; off, the stereo of both is ignored

label: Precursor tolerance
text: Library precursor against the precursor of the feature

label: Fragment tolerance
text: Fragment window in Da; 0 follows the query: 0.02 Da, or 0.5 Da for a unit-resolution file.

label: Decoy tolerance
text: A decoy lies beyond this many ppm of every true delta, and a row matches a decoy within it

label: Mass tolerance of an arc
text: Largest error of the observed difference of m/z against the mass of the change of formula

label: Fragment tolerance
text: Matching of the fragments with the cleavages of the parent (HR spectra)

label: Fewest informative fragments
text: Fewer informative fragments cannot tell one class from the others

label: Informative fragment
text: A fragment is informative from this share of the base peak, if its formula is within 5 ppm
